Appearance:
MR JM BAROT(143) for the Appellant(s) No. 1,2,3,4 MR DAKSHESH MEHTA(2430) for the Defendant(s) No. 3 MR.KIRIT R CHAUDHARI(3745) for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2 ==========================================================

sentences.text:
The present First Appeal is preferred by the appellants - original claimants, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 06.05.2010 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary), Mehsana in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.778 of 2008, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,42,000/-
with 7.5% interest per annum to the claimants, holding the opponents i.e. owner, driver and insurance company liable, jointly and severally.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.778 of 2008
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 On 18.10.2008, the deceased- Ganpatbhai Karshanbhai Patel was traveling on his motorcycle bearing No.GJ-2-AH- Legal Heirs Of Ganpatbhai Karshanbhai ... vs Raval Pravinbhai Bhikhabhai on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196725325/
1 7251 from Balol village to Parama and was standing on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined left side of the road in Balol village, when the offending vehicle was returning from Bahuchraji hit the deceased- Ganpatbhai Karshanbhai Patel and thereby,
the deceased died on the spot.
2.2

Thereafter, the widow of the deceased, daughters of the deceased aged about 16 and 11 respectively as well as son of the deceased aged 5 years preferred the claim petition before the concerned tribunal for compensation.
2.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal has been preferred by claimants before this Court for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard learned advocate Mr. J.M. Barot for the appellants and learned advocate Mr. Dakshesh Mehta for the respondent No.3-Insurance Company.

Learned advocate Mr. Kirit R. Chaudhari appears on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 and 2.
3.1

Learned advocate Mr. J.M. Barot for the appellants has submitted that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is contrary to the evidence available on the record and tribunal wrongly held that the deceased was liable for the accident for 40%, though the respondent driver of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined offending vehicle is absolutely liable for the accident.

He has further submitted that while awarding the award the tribunal should have considered the future and prospective income of the deceased and the tribunal has not considered the prospective income of the deceased and thereby, erred in passing the award for compensation.
3.2
He has further submitted that the tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- as the future income of the deceased would be on higher stand.

It is further submitted by the learned advocate for the appellants that the tribunal ought to have considered the aspect that the deceased was the sole earner of the family and much more amount was to be awarded under various heads viz. Expectation of life, love and affection as well as transportation and funeral expenses.

He has submitted that age of the legal heirs and deceased is required to be considered in case of fatal accident and multiplier should be given accordingly, but in the present case, tribunal has erred in multiplier and thereby, awarded less amount of compensation.

3.3 He has further submitted that the tribunal erred in holding the deceased 40% liable, wherein,
looking to the Panchnama of the place of accident, it is crystal clear that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving in rash and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011 ORDER DATED:
12/06/2024 undefined negligent manner, which resulted into the death of the deceased.

It is submitted by the learned advocate that the tribunal erred in holding that the motorcycle of the deceased is damaged from the front side, whereas, the deceased was stationary at the time of the accident and the jeep driven by the driver came from wrong side and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased from the right side resulting death of the deceased.
Therefore, he has prayed to allow the present appeal by enhancing the amount of compensation.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned advocate Mr. learned advocate Mr. Dakshesh Mehta submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, as the Tribunal has considered all the aspects and passed the impugned judgment and award after considering the material available on the record.

However, from the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellants that the Tribunal has committed certain errors, on this aspect, learned advocate for the respondent No.3 has submitted that, if it transpires to this Court that there is some error in calculation of the amount, while awarding compensation by the Tribunal, then the Court may pass appropriate order by considering the submissions made on behalf of the appellants, in the interest of justice.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined 5.
I have considered the submissions made by the respective parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
5.1 It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.

5.2 It transpires from the record that the tribunal has awarded compensation, whereby, the tribunal has not properly considered various aspects regarding the future loss of income and also, committed error in considering the multiplier 15, as the age of the deceased was 43 years and as per the ratio laid down by judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation reported NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined in (2009) 6 SCC 121, multiplier ought to have been considered 14 instead of 15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation reported NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The tribunal has committed error in considering only Rs.3000/- as monthly income, which ought to have been considered by adding 25% of prospective income i.e. Rs.750/- and therefore, Rs.3,750/- is the future prospective income, whereby, 25% of the amount is required to be deducted towards personal expenses, therefore, the income for calculation is required to be considered as Rs.2812/-
per month which is required to be multiplied by 12 months and also with 14 multiplier which comes to Rs.4,72,416/-.
5.3 The deceased has four dependents; the widow wife, two minor daughters and one son at the time of accident.

The tribunal has awarded only Rs.20,000/- towards the loss of consortium, which as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram and Ors reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, ought to have been considered Rs.40,000/- per person, plus by adding 10% increase for two years, so that will come to Rs.48,000/-, so for four persons it will come to the tune of Rs.1,92,000/-, which ought to have been awarded under the head of loss of consortium.

3 head of funeral expenses, which ought to have been considered Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- ought to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1633/2011 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined have been awarded towards loss of estate, so total of Rs.30,000/- under the head of conventional amount and therefore, considering the above mentioned calculations, the appellants - claimants are entitled to get the following final amount as compensation:

Sr.No. Particulars Amounts (Rs.)
1. Future loss of income 4,72,416/-

2 . Loss of consortium 1,92,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- per person   10% increase for two years)
3. Loss of estate 15,000/-
4. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Total 6,94,416/-
5.4

The tribunal has awarded Rs.3,42,000/-, therefo further enhanced amount of compensation i.e. Rs.3,52,416/- is required to be awarded with 7.5%
interest to the appellants - claimants.

Therefore, the present appeal is required to be allowed considering the judgments of Sarla Verma (supra) and National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16SCC 680 as well as Magma General (supra) and the amount is required to be enhanced.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the present appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent by enhancing the amount awarded by the tribunal, which is to the tune of Rs.3,42,000/- and now, which is enhanced to the tune of Rs.6,94,416/-.
Therefore, the enhanced amount of Rs.3,52,416/- is required to be deposited by the respondent No.3 with 7.5% interest from the date of claim petition.

Therefore, the respondent No.3-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.3,52,416/- with 7.5%
interest per annum from the date of claim petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary), Mehsana, within a period of one month from today.

6.1 On deposition of such amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount (including the enhanced amount) lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque or by way of transfer in the bank account of the claimants, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
